info.description:
Post to your BrightBean channels from scripts, Zapier, n8n or your own agent.

## Getting started
Every path below is under `https://api-platform.brightbean.xyz`. Check your key with:
```
curl https://api-platform.brightbean.xyz/api/v1/me/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "User-Agent: my-agent/1.0"
```
Bodies are JSON. Times are ISO 8601 with an offset (`2026-10-06T09:00:00+02:00`). Ids are UUIDs. A list path works with or without its trailing slash (`/api/v1/posts/` or `/api/v1/posts`).

**Send a User-Agent naming your client.** The API sits behind Cloudflare, which blocks Python's built-in default (`Python-urllib/3.x`) with a plain-text `403 error code: 1010` before the request reaches BrightBean. Any value of your own gets through. `requests`, `httpx`, curl, Node, Go and Java clients already send one that does.

## Keys
Create a key in BrightBean under Settings → Workspace → API & MCP. Send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key belongs to one workspace, may use only the channels picked for it, and can do only what its permissions allow AND what the person who made it can still do. Revoking a key stops it within 60 seconds.

Permissions: `read` (Read channels and posts), `create_posts` (Create drafts and send for approval), `upload_media` (Upload media), `view_analytics` (Read analytics), `publish_directly` (Publish and schedule without approval). Without `publish_directly`, or when the workspace requires approval for everyone, a post you ask to schedule or publish goes to Review in BrightBean, labelled with your key, and is carried out once someone approves it. The `routed` field says which happened.

## Errors
Every error from the API is `{ "error": "<code>", "detail": "<what went wrong>" }`:
- 401: missing, invalid, expired or revoked key.
- 403: `missing permission: <permission>`, or a channel this key may not post to.
- 404: not found, including any post on a channel this key can't see.
- 409: the post is in the wrong state (editing one waiting for approval: withdraw it first), or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running.
- 422: the content won't work: over a channel's limit, a first comment where a channel can't take one, a time without an offset or in the past, a channel's daily cap for that time (`available_at` says when it fits).
- 405: wrong method for that path (`Allow` says which).
- 413: the body is too large.
- 429: too many requests (`tier`, `retry_after`, and a Retry-After header), or a channel's daily cap when publishing now.
- 503: a temporary failure while handling an upload. Retry the same request.

A 403 with a plain-text body `error code: 1010` comes from Cloudflare, not the API: send your own User-Agent (see Getting started).

## Limits
Per key, per minute: 120 writes and 300 reads. Per workspace: 1000 writes a minute. Windows are 60 seconds and counted per Cloudflare location.

## Retries
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (or `idempotencyKey` in the body) on writes. Repeating a request with the same key within 24 hours never repeats the work; the same key with a different body is a 422.

## Uploading media
1. `POST /api/v1/media/uploads` with the file's type and size. The answer holds URLs for the first parts (up to 8) and `partCount`.
2. `PUT` each part's bytes (`partSize` each, the last one smaller) to its URL and keep the ETag header each answer returns.
3. For a file with more parts, `POST /api/v1/media/uploads/{id}/parts` for up to 16 more URLs at a time. A URL expires, so ask for them as you go.
4. `POST /api/v1/media/uploads/{id}/complete` with every part's number and ETag. Use the returned id in `mediaAssetIds`.

## Polling for changes
`GET /api/v1/posts/` and `GET /api/v1/posts/{id}` return an ETag. Send it back as `If-None-Match`: when nothing changed the answer is `304` and costs almost nothing. Or pass the previous response's `serverTime` as `updatedSince`. Changes can take up to a minute to show. Deleted posts are not reported by `updatedSince`; they answer 404.

## Activity
Every call is logged under the key's Activity in Settings, without request bodies. Activity and "last used" can take up to 20 minutes to appear.

## MCP
The MCP server is `https://api-platform.brightbean.xyz/api/v1/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, `POST`). It has the same permissions, limits and Activity log as REST.
- **With an API key:** send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, e.g. `claude mcp add --transport http brightbean https://api-platform.brightbean.xyz/api/v1/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>"`.
- **With OAuth** (claude.ai, Claude Desktop): add the URL as a custom connector. The client finds everything from the `401`: discovery is at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1/mcp`, and the endpoints are `/oauth/authorize/`, `/oauth/token/`, `/oauth/register` (dynamic client registration) and `/oauth/revoke_token/`. PKCE (`S256`) is required. The person approving picks the workspace, channels and permissions.

proposedPublishAt.description: A proposed publish time for the draft (ISO 8601 with an offset). A note only: nothing is queued, scheduled or published because of it, and scheduling, queueing or publishing the post clears it. A `delivery` in the same call wins: carried out directly, the proposal ends up empty; sent to Review with a time, the proposal becomes that time. `null` means none.

post.description: The copy keeps the words, media, channels and per-channel settings, and starts as a draft with no schedule and no approval. The original is not changed. Channels that can no longer be posted to are left out and listed in `droppedChannels`; a partially published post keeps only the channels that didn't go out. TikTok settings are not copied: TikTok requires them to be chosen for every post. It never schedules or publishes.

idempotencyKey.description: Retrying with the same key never repeats the work. Also accepted as the Idempotency-Key header.

droppedChannels.description: Channels of the original the copy left out, because they can't be posted to.

keptFailedOnly.description: True when the original was partially published: the copy leaves out the channels that published, and keeps the ones that failed or never went out.
